name: Samoan siva and fagufagu (Polynesian dance-song)
lineage: Samoan siva (formal dance) and fagufagu (drum-led collective dance) Polynesian-cultural-performance traditions of the Samoan archipelago (Independent State of Samoa and American Samoa). The siva manaia is the standard performance featuring a single dancer (often the daughter of the host family in a fa'alavelave ceremonial gathering) accompanied by sung verses and slit-drum (pate) and rolled-mat (papa) percussion. The taualuga formal high-chief's-dance is the culminating ceremonial-form. Vocal repertoire features distinct fa'aluga (verse) and fa'amalama (refrain) structural sections. The post-twentieth-century Pacific-festival circuit and Polynesian Cultural Center anchor international circulation.
